book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Disparage small country with some demur

parts.note: a land is a country or nation
er is the sound of a slight hesitation, a small demur

explanation.surface: Someone sniffily talks down a tiny nation while voicing a few reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander someone is to make false, damaging statements that belittle their reputation.

clue.text: Top water-sports champ

parts.note: surf, riding waves, stands for water sports
an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: The best surfer or swimmer around.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface is the uppermost layer or face of something, its top.

clue.text: A couple of fellows talented and friendly

parts.note: taken as written
F is fellow, so two of them give FF
able means skilled, talented

explanation.surface: Two gifted, pleasant chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means pleasant and easy to talk to, a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: Leaving arid area to which no-one returns

parts.note: a desert is a dry, barren area

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: no plus I, the Roman one

explanation.surface: Quitting a barren wasteland nobody ever goes back to.
explanation.definitionFit: Desertion is the act of abandoning a person, post or place, a form of leaving.

clue.text: Let out to let again

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to lease is to let property

explanation.surface: A property let afresh, or freed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' reads as renting a property, matching 'let again', but it means set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a prisoner or animal is to let it go free.

clue.text: Continue supporting articulate tennis ace

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: to articulate is to speak out, so a word is given by how it is said

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis draw

explanation.surface: A backer urges a well-spoken tennis star to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis a seed is one of the top-ranked players placed to avoid meeting early.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to go on or carry on with a course of action, a synonym of continue.

clue.text: Delivery charge fixed after many years

parts.note: to post a notice is to fix it up on a board or wall
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Shipping costs were set after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee paid for sending mail, the cost of delivery.

clue.text: More than ten initially seen in public

parts.note: over means more than

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the word ten supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: A crowd of more than ten seen out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden, so in public view.

clue.text: Beg English knight to negotiate

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
to treat is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: Appealing to an English knight to broker a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead with someone earnestly, to implore or beg.

clue.text: Ridiculed when free to enter action

indicators.note: to enter means to go into, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: Mocked when let loose to join the fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Derided means mocked or laughed at with contempt, much as ridiculed.

clue.text: Umpire gets regular, heartless rejection

parts.note: ref, short for referee, an official like an umpire

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the word is cut out

parts.note: usual means normal, regular

explanation.surface: An official gets a habitual, cold-hearted turning down.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is the act of declining or turning something down, a synonym of rejection.

clue.text: Jumper showing signs of exertion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted pullover, which Britons call a jumper
second meaning: one who sweats, perspiring from effort

explanation.walkthrough: A jumper in British English is a knitted top, not someone who leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a knitted pullover and, literally, a person perspiring from hard physical work.

clue.text: A physician to HM put in the shade

parts.note: taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
Her Majesty, the Queen, is ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A royal doctor ends up overshadowed in someone else's glory.
explanation.walkthrough: MB is the British medical degree Bachelor of Medicine, so stands for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange colour, one particular shade.

clue.text: A role he and I had in racial segregation

parts.note: taken as written
a part is a role in a play
taken as written
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the part two people played under an unjust regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was the South African system of enforced separation of people by race.

clue.text: Solitary child follows oriental soldiers

indicators.note: the child comes after the soldiers in the answer

parts.note: E for eastern, oriental
RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A lonely youngster trails behind a troop from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious recluse or hermit, so a solitary person.

clue.text: Thrilled when last spouse gets summoned

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
cited means called to appear in court

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted that a former partner has been called to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited means eager and stirred up with pleasure, much the same as thrilled.

clue.text: Criminal gets angry inside when deceived

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece is placed in the middle of the other

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
heated means angry or impassioned

explanation.surface: A crook boils with rage after being tricked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' suggests a criminal in prison, but it puts one piece within another.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheated on is to have a partner be unfaithful, deceived in a relationship.

clue.text: Aunt set out to register complaint

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aunt sets off to lodge a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance, but here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial disease, and complaint is a standard word for an ailment.

clue.text: First found among most of these believers

indicators.note: found among means placed inside, so one piece goes in the other
most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened
1st, the abbreviation for first, read as IST

explanation.surface: The leading example appears among the bulk of these faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: First as 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I, is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Theists are people who believe in the existence of a god or gods.

clue.text: Removal of mattress cover results in reprimand

parts.note: ticking, or tick, is the fabric case of a mattress
off means taken away, removed

explanation.surface: Stripping the bed's cover gets someone told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is an informal British phrase for scold or rebuke.

clue.text: Pay to get remains of tree taken out

parts.note: a stump is what is left of a felled tree
a stump taken out is pulled up from the ground

explanation.surface: Paying to have a tree's remnants dug out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump up is an informal British phrase for paying what is due, often reluctantly.

clue.text: What barbers give to get company commission?

parts.note: a crew is a company of workers
a cut is a share or commission

explanation.surface: Is a haircut how barbers win a firm's business?
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short haircut, a service a barber provides.

clue.text: Eric and Mac make pottery

indicators.note: make means form or shape, so the letters are formed into something new

parts.note: the letters of the name are rearranged
the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two friends throw pots together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic denotes pottery or other articles of fired clay.

clue.text: Drive used car following repairs

indicators.note: repairs means mending, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking a second-hand car out after it has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like motoring, but it means a vigorous campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is an energetic campaign for a cause, which a drive also is.

clue.text: The check made in that place

parts.note: taken as written
a rein is a check or restraint

explanation.surface: A cheque was written there.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal adverb meaning inside or within that place or thing.

clue.text: Former PM's home endlessly needed state funds

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence

explanation.surface: An ex-premier's residence badly needed public money.
explanation.walkthrough: Chequers is the country house in Buckinghamshire kept for the UK Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the British treasury, the government's public money.

clue.text: Standing upright before going to court

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Rising to one's feet before heading to a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means vertical, upright, straight up.

clue.text: Many involved in genuine cease-fire

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: true means real, genuine
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: Lots of people take part in a real end to fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreement between enemies to stop fighting, a ceasefire.

clue.text: Orpheus direly needed support

indicators.note: direly means terribly, so the name is wrecked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: The mythical musician desperately needed someone to prop him up.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore up is to prop something with beams, or to reinforce or bolster it.

clue.text: Intervene to make communicators take note

indicators.note: take means the press picks up the note, adding it at the end

parts.note: the media are the means of mass communication
te is a note of the sol-fa scale, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: Stepping in to get the press to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to step into a dispute to reconcile the parties, a form of intervening.

clue.text: A car frequently coming in close

indicators.note: coming in means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to stop is to close or shut off
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A vehicle often drawing up nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft-top is a convertible car with a folding fabric roof.

clue.text: Interest in business

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something of interest or worry to one
second meaning: a firm or company

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like one phrase about a stake in a firm; each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a matter that engages someone's attention and a commercial firm or enterprise.
